subject.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane

question: Should Active Memory permit one concurrent recall per agent without an additional process-wide aggregate cap?
rationale: Source and live proof establish that per-agent lanes solve cross-agent queueing, but neither tests nor the three-agent deployment determine the desired resource ceiling for larger gateways.

options.title: Accept per-agent concurrency
options.body: Land this narrow fix and monitor or separately track an aggregate limit if larger deployments show saturation.

options.title: Require an aggregate cap
options.body: Pause merge until Active Memory composes per-agent serialization with a gateway-wide concurrency limiter and focused multi-agent tests.

recommendation.title: Accept per-agent concurrency
recommendation.body: Land this narrow fix and monitor or separately track an aggregate limit if larger deployments show saturation.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the dedicated-lane behavior that defines the concurrency boundary this PR changes.
